question: Grapefruit juice increases fexofenadine blood levels by inhibiting its hepatic CYP3A4 metabolism, similar to its well-known interaction with statins.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Grapefruit juice does NOT increase fexofenadine levels. Unlike most CYP3A4 substrates (statins, ciclosporin), fexofenadine depends on intestinal OATP transporters for absorption. Fruit juices (grapefruit, apple, orange) inhibit these OATP transporters, reducing fexofenadine bioavailability by up to 36–73% — leading to apparent treatment failure. Counsel patients to take fexofenadine with water, not fruit juice.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. This is a counter-intuitive interaction: grapefruit, apple, and orange juices actually DECREASE fexofenadine bioavailability (by up to 36–73%) by inhibiting intestinal OATP (organic anion transporting polypeptide) transporters. Unlike the CYP3A4-mediated interaction that raises statin levels, fexofenadine depends on OATP for gut uptake, so juice inhibition REDUCES absorption. Patients should take fexofenadine with water only.
